chunks: Zurārah ibn Aʿyan narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

If a person in ihram in the Haram strikes a pigeon or anything up to the size of a gazelle, then a damm is due from him which he sheds, and he also gives in charity the equivalent of its price. But if he strikes any of that while he is halal, then he must give in charity the equivalent of its price.

key_terms.الظَّبْيَ: a gazelle, indicating the upper size range in this ruling
key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the Sacred Precinct in which hunting is prohibited
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: a person in the state of ihram during hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.حَلَالٌ: not in the state of ihram
key_terms.حَمَامَةً: a pigeon, mentioned as a type of hunted game
key_terms.دَمٌ: a sacrificial animal or blood-compensation due as a penalty
key_terms.يَتَصَدَّقُ: he gives charity as financial compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for killing game in the Haram while in a state of ihram or while not in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about hunting game within the Sacred Precinct while in ihram and outside ihram. It distinguishes between the muhrim and the non-muhrim in the Haram, requiring a sacrificial penalty and charity for the former, and monetary charity for the latter.
